findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
The legacy history cap is measured in characters, but JSON escapes each non-BMP character as 12 ASCII bytes. An earlier release's retained history containing 8,000 emoji produces a `legacy_text` field of about 96 KB by itself. `_compact` eventually runs out of timestamped rows and exits while the record is oversized; `_bounded_body` cannot remove that field. The resulting pull request body exceeds GitHub's 64 KB limit, so the stated fixed-size outcome is unmet.
findings.title: Not done: Legacy Unicode history can exceed the pull request body limit

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
When repeated closes make the latest round exceed the budget, the fallback cut folds every row through the last timestamp, including an open `owner wait start`. The summary stores elapsed totals but no pending wait ID. On a fresh clone, `pending_merge_wait()` finds no start to end, and `merged()` measures time after the cut without a waiting span. The board then labels the remaining human merge wait as unknown, and a later close can start a second wait. The repeated-close proof does not exercise an open owner wait.
findings.title: Folding an open owner wait loses its remaining waiting time
